subject.title: fix(cli): cap config patch file input

question: Should `openclaw config patch --file` reject existing patch files above 1 MiB so it matches the current stdin input boundary?
rationale: The bounded loop is technically sound, but this intentionally tightens a public CLI workflow and can stop existing oversized-file automation at runtime.

options.title: Adopt file/stdin parity
options.body: Merge the PR and make both config-patch input modes reject payloads above 1 MiB before parsing or writes.

options.title: Keep file input uncapped
options.body: Do not merge this behavior change until maintainers choose a compatibility-preserving policy for large patch files.

recommendation.title: Adopt file/stdin parity
recommendation.body: Merge the PR and make both config-patch input modes reject payloads above 1 MiB before parsing or writes.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the only concrete participant tied to the current implementation and can clarify the intended compatibility boundary, though a core CLI owner should make the final policy call.
